title: helm(private): enhance private values schema, init hooks, CRD validation and upgrade/rollback notes
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Improve the Helm chart for Redwood Private by tightening the values schema for the private installer, improving templating for CRD validation, making init jobs and hooks more robust for upgrades and rollbacks, and adding clear upgrade/rollback instructions.

Motivation: customers running Private (VPC/on-prem) saw repeated install-time failures when CRDs were partially applied and when the legacy init job retried against a partially available KMS/Secrets backend. This PR standardizes the values schema (explicitly typed fields + defaults), adds templating guards to avoid rendering invalid CRs, converts several init tasks from a single monolithic job to smaller, idempotent hook jobs, and documents upgrade/rollback steps to reduce operator error.

Changes:
- values.schema.json: expanded the JSON schema for values.yaml to include strict types for persistence, k8sSecrets, kms config, and network policies; added descriptions and default examples.
- templates/crds/*.yaml: added explicit apiVersion checks and conditional rendering (only render CRs when crd.enabled == true and crd.version is compatible).
- templates/hooks/init-secrets-job.yaml / init-registrations-hook.yaml: split initial provisioning into two hooks (pre-install: create-namespaces-and-secrets, post-install: register-cluster) with proper helm.sh/hook-weight to ensure deterministic order. Hooks are now idempotent and tolerate partial failures by using annotations to mark successful subtasks.
- templates/_helpers.tpl: new helper funcs for safeToDeploy and semverCompare to gate resources during upgrades.
- tests/helm/upgrade-rollback.md: added explicit manual and CI-driven upgrade/rollback playbook with sample helm commands and expected states.
- NOTES.txt: expanded with migration notes and new configuration knobs (persistence.storageClass, kms.provider, network.allowedCIDRs).
- chart.yaml: bumped chart version to 2.7.0 and added maintainers list.

Commits (high level): ["split init job into idempotent hooks", "add values.schema.json and validate in CI", "gate CRD templates with schema checks", "document upgrade/rollback and add e2e helm test"]

Files changed (high level): ["charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json", "charts/redwood-private/values.yaml (example)", "charts/redwood-private/templates/hooks/*", "charts/redwood-private/templates/crds/*", "charts/redwood-private/templates/_helpers.tpl", "charts/redwood-private/NOTES.txt", "charts/redwood-private/Chart.yaml", "charts/redwood-private/tests/upgrade-rollback.md"]

Migration notes (included in NOTES.txt string):
- Before upgrading, ensure crd.enabled=true and that all CRDs are present in the cluster (kubectl get crd redwoodclusters.redwood.io).
- If you use an external KMS, pre-populate kms.provider credentials into a sealed secret or pass via --set-file during upgrade.
- To perform a safe upgrade: helm upgrade --install redwood-private charts/redwood-private --namespace redwood --wait --atomic --values myvalues.yaml
- If an init hook fails, check release hooks with kubectl get jobs -n redwood -l "helm.sh/hook" and investigate the annotated subtask outputs.

Rollback notes:
- Because hooks perform provisioning, rollback should be done with care. Run helm rollback <release> <revision> and then run scripts/tests/verify-rollback.sh from the chart tests to validate cluster state.
- If CR resources were partially created, use kustomize/kubectl to delete offending CRs before rollback; the hooks are idempotent and will reprovision on a re-install.

Testing:
- Added helm lint + schema validate step in CI; chart is validated with helm schema test during CI.
- Added an integration CI job (integration:private-install) that performs install -> upgrade -> rollback on a KinD cluster using example values.
- Manual test instructions included in charts/redwood-private/tests/upgrade-rollback.md

Review notes: reviewers asked for a migration flag to opt-out of new semantics; added values.featureFlags.enableInitHooks boolean (default true) to let operators disable the new hook flow during staged rollouts.

Security: secrets are now only templated into sealed secret manifests when values.k8sSecrets.seal == true; otherwise the chart emits instructions only.

Backwards compatibility: Default values preserve previous behaviour where possible; CRD gating is opt-in via crd.strictValidation (default false) to avoid breaking older clusters. See release notes below.

chore(templates): gate CRD rendering with semver checks
docs: add upgrade/rollback playbook and NOTES expansion

ci_summary: All checks passing after one forced re-run of the integration job (KinD flakiness). Helm lint and schema validation added to prevent regressions.
release_notes: charts/redwood-private v2.7.0: tighten values schema for private installer (values.schema.json)
Introduce idempotent pre-install and post-install hooks for init tasks to reduce install-time flakiness
Add semver gating and conditional rendering for CRD templates (opt-in via crd.strictValidation)
Documented upgrade and rollback procedures and added CI tests for install->upgrade->rollback flow
notes_for_ops: If you operate with an external KMS, preload credentials before upgrade.
If upgrading from <2.6.0, consider setting values.featureFlags.enableInitHooks=false to stage the rollout.
Use helm --atomic --wait for upgrades to ensure hooks finish or the release is rolled back automatically.
